findings.title: Retry budget depends entirely on broker-supplied delivery_count; missing/stale count loops forever
findings.evidence: attempts is computed once as _delivery_attempts(message) + 1 and nothing in the worker ever increments a local counter; on failure the code calls queue.nack(message) and continues, so if the broker does not bump delivery_count (default 0 is used when the attribute is absent or unparsable, per _delivery_attempts) attempts stays 1 and the message is nacked and re-received indefinitely, never reaching MAX_ATTEMPTS and never dead-lettered.
findings.recommendation: Track attempts locally (e.g. keep the incremented count on the requeued message, or hold a per-message in-process counter keyed by message id) and dead-letter once the local budget is exhausted, so dead-lettering does not depend on the broker mutating delivery_count. Alternatively assert/require the attribute and fail fast when it is absent.

findings.title: Ack calls are outside the try blocks: an ack failure aborts the batch and duplicates side effects
findings.evidence: Both queue.ack(message) calls sit outside any try/except (after dlq.send and in the success else-branch), so an ack exception propagates out of process_messages: the outcome counters are lost, and on redelivery the handler runs again after its side effects already committed (or the message is dead-lettered a second time).
findings.recommendation: Wrap the ack calls so a failed ack is logged and the message left for redelivery without aborting the whole loop, and make handler side effects idempotent or document at-least-once semantics explicitly.

findings.title: Message already at or past the attempt budget is still executed once more
findings.evidence: The check is only attempts < MAX_ATTEMPTS after the handler has already run; a message redelivered with delivery_count already at MAX_ATTEMPTS or greater is handed to handler(message.body) one extra time before being dead-lettered.
findings.recommendation: Check the delivery count before invoking the handler and send straight to the DLQ when the budget is already exhausted.

findings.title: Dead-letter send failures are only logged, never counted or surfaced to the caller
findings.evidence: On a failed dlq.send the code logs and continues without nacking and without incrementing any failure counter; the returned dict only has processed and dead_lettered, so the caller cannot tell a drained queue from one where messages were abandoned or are being re-received in a tight loop.
findings.recommendation: Add a failed/dead_letter_failed counter to the return value and explicitly nack (or otherwise bound the retry) on DLQ send failure so the loop cannot spin on the same message.

findings.title: No tests exercise the retry, dead-letter, or ack-failure branches
findings.evidence: The change adds a new worker with MAX_ATTEMPTS retry logic and no tests were run or added; the two riskiest paths (nack-then-success, dlq.send failure, ack failure) are uncovered.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests with a fake queue/DLQ covering: success on first attempt, success after retries, dead-letter at the attempt limit, dlq.send raising, ack raising, and a message with missing delivery_count.
